summary: Comprehensive backend regression tests written for NexusERP PME covering auth+RBAC, leads CRUD+scoping+messages, WhatsApp webhook (token validation + upsert + append) + simulate, products (admin-only writes), customers (LGPD consent + anonymize + from_lead), orders (create+add/remove items+list+scoping), payments (add+mark_paid), invoicing (NFE tax decomposition 32.25% and NFSE 14.25%), dashboard KPIs/monthly/tax_breakdown/receivables, and full E2E flow WA->lead->customer->order->payment->invoice->dashboard delta. Found 1 CRITICAL bug in Order.number column (no Postgres sequence) which blocked all orders/payments/invoicing/dashboard flows; applied a workaround inside the router so remaining tests pass. Final: 18/18 tests pass.

critical.issue: Order.number is defined in models.py as `Integer, autoincrement=True, unique=True, nullable=False`. In SQLAlchemy, autoincrement only applies to primary keys; since `id` is the PK (String UUID), no Postgres SEQUENCE is created for `number`. Every INSERT into orders sent NULL for number -> asyncpg NotNullViolationError -> 500. Applied a workaround (compute next number via SELECT MAX(number)+1 in routers/orders_router.py::_next_order_number). Proper fix: attach an explicit `Sequence('orders_number_seq')` to the column and CREATE SEQUENCE in DB (or run ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN number ADD GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY). The workaround is race-condition-prone under concurrent order creation.

minor.issue: CORSMiddleware uses `allow_origins=['*']` (default) with `allow_credentials=False`. If in the future the frontend needs cookies/credentials, this must be explicit origins list.

Dev helper endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED. It can create leads/messages without any auth token and is exposed via the public /api. Should require admin or at least any authenticated user, or be gated by an env flag/DEBUG mode.
Pydantic v2 EmailStr rejects reserved TLDs like .test / .example. Not necessarily a bug but worth noting for docs/tests: user-facing error is 422 which is fine.

The 'last 6 months' calculation uses `now.replace(day=1) - timedelta(days=30*i)` which is imprecise around month boundaries (e.g., can produce duplicate months or miss one). Should use dateutil.relativedelta or manual year/month arithmetic.

Uses CustomerIn (all-or-nothing) as the update payload instead of an Optional-fields update schema, so a partial update requires resending every field. Consider a CustomerUpdate schema like LeadUpdate.

_recalc computes total_net = total_gross - total_taxes; when an item is added/removed AFTER an invoice was issued, total_taxes is not recomputed so total_net can become inconsistent. Consider blocking item mutations once status='invoiced'.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the critical bug: models.py::Order.number uses SQLAlchemy `Integer, autoincrement=True` on a non-primary-key column. SQLAlchemy documents that autoincrement is only applied to the single-column integer PK; on any other column it is silently ignored. Postgres therefore did NOT create a sequence for the column, and every ORM INSERT (which omits `number` from the INSERT list because it has no server_default) sent NULL, violating NOT NULL. Reproduction: POST /api/orders with any valid customer -> 500 asyncpg NotNullViolationError. Mitigation applied: compute MAX(number)+1 at insert time. Permanent fix: define `Sequence('orders_number_seq')` on the column (SQLAlchemy will emit CREATE SEQUENCE and use nextval) OR use `Identity()` / `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY`. Existing DB requires a manual ALTER since create_all skips existing tables.
